objective: Decide what the online renewal flow must show so residents know a renewal succeeded.

research_questions.question: How do residents confirm that a renewal succeeded?
What keeps residents from renewing online?

methodology_note: Two fictional accounts. Counts describe the fixture, not a population.

participants.note: Two fictional residents. The P1 follow up adds a source, not a participant.

executive_summary.lead: Proof of payment ended the task.
executive_summary.detail: Two of two residents looked for a receipt or bank record before they relaxed.
One of two chose the counter because of the website.

themes.headline: Residents looked for proof of payment before they considered the renewal done

blocks.label: Pattern
blocks.text: P1 checked a bank app; P2 waited for a printed receipt.

blocks.label: Implication
blocks.text: Confirmation needs to be immediate and unambiguous.

quotes.text: I wasn't sure the payment went through, so I checked my bank app twice.
The clerk printed a receipt right away, so I knew it was done.

themes.callout: T1   2 of 2 residents fit the pattern.

themes.headline: Distrust of the website kept one resident at the counter

blocks.label: Pattern
blocks.text: P2 did not trust the website with a card.

quotes.text: I went to the counter because I didn't trust [the city] website with my card.

themes.callout: T2   1 of 2 residents. A weak signal.

opportunities.title: Immediate confirmation
opportunities.detail: Residents relaxed only once they held proof.
directions: Show an on-screen receipt at once.

limitations: Two invented accounts. Retrospective interviews do not establish task success or prevalence.
